summary: Governed restoration of an already reserved ticket (issue 509)

delivery.outcome: An already reserved ticket whose canonical checkout, branch or uncommitted metadata was lost is restored under the same identity through new-ticket.sh --restore-request, bound to its reservation, exact head, pinned snapshot and live controller lease, without granting editing or merge authority.
nonGoals: No new ticket number, high-water change or reuse
No owner handoff: the controller performs it before restoration
No material source restoration and no change to ticket_recovery.py

architecture.decision: A separate managed helper scripts/ticket_restoration.py reuses ticket_recovery's safe loading, controller lock and diagnostics. It requires number <= high-water, a unique .subactor/leases reservation naming the same owner, a SHA-256-pinned README.md+intent.json snapshot and an active unexpired controller lease in phase claimed or editing; it creates only the missing branch (create-only update-ref), the relative canonical worktree and the two metadata files (link, never overwrite), and is idempotent on rerun. new-ticket.sh routes --restore-request through the existing recovery block so all exclusions apply.
architecture.rollback: Revert the commit; --restore-request disappears and recovery behaves as before.
